natural_language_rule: In general, apps may post no more than one message per second per channel. [...] We allow bursts over that limit for short periods.
context: Slack Web API rate limits documentation (docs.slack.dev; redirected from api.slack.com), special limit for posting messages. The page also defines per-method tiers (Tier 1: 1+/min, Tier 2: 20+/min, Tier 3: 50+/min, Tier 4: 100+/min).
vague_quantifier: 'In general' + 'We allow bursts over that limit for short periods' -- an un-quantified burst allowance around an exact 1 msg/sec/channel anchor
formal_anchor: 1 message / second / channel (documented posting limit); the strict reading maps to the tightest per-window cap in the pool

formal_source.license: official documentation, quoted under fair use for research

harness_mapping.metered_action: one billed gpt-4o-mini call = one posted message
harness_mapping.window: one channel session = one episode (W=12 posting opportunities)
harness_mapping.axis: calls (running count of paid posts in the window)
harness_mapping.reading_form: psi_k := forbid posting once >= k messages already posted in the window (calls >= k)
harness_mapping.note: calls-per-window quota framing (primary per task); each paid call is the metered posting action. Nested caps k tight->loose give an interval retained band; the strict 1 msg/sec anchor maps to the tightest cap (post-clarify target).
